# CLI reference

Every command's `--help`, as printed. `qda` builds and inspects checkpoints, `qda-kl` scores them against the original model, `qda-agent` runs the search (`prepare`, `search`, `status`).

**Stability.** For scripts that call these commands (`qda` `build`, `plan`, `doctor`, `inspect`, `eval`, `export`, `decode-gguf`, `fisher`, `calib`, `rotate-draft`, `sensitivity`, `traces`; `qda-kl` `ref`, `score`, `kl`, `gencheck`; `qda-agent` `prepare`, `search`, `status`, `run`, `gate`, `cand0`): in 0.1.x each command and its flags keep their name and meaning. Changing one takes a new minor version and is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/humanfia/qda/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Output text and messages may change.

## `qda`

```text
usage: qda [-h]
           {build,plan,doctor,inspect,eval,export,decode-gguf,fisher,calib,rotate-draft,sensitivity,traces}
           ...

Build checkpoints from a config file, and tools that work on checkpoints.

positional arguments:
  {build,plan,doctor,inspect,eval,export,decode-gguf,fisher,calib,rotate-draft,sensitivity,traces}
    build               build a checkpoint
    plan                print the plan or the refusal; no GPU work
    doctor              run the checks the commands refuse on, early; --report lists the
                        environment
    fisher              per-unit bits and predicted dKL for each menu format (diagonal Fisher),
                        and an allocation
    inspect             say what a checkpoint is, what it lacks and whether it serves as is
    calib               make calibration files for one model
    export              copy a checkpoint without its run records, hashed and read back
    sensitivity         GGUF class weight bytes and a type allocation from reads
    decode-gguf         decode a GGUF back to a servable HF checkpoint
    eval                score checkpoints against one reference, one JSON per (checkpoint, suite
                        part)
    rotate-draft        rotate a speculative-decoding draft into a rotated checkpoint's residual
                        basis
    traces              a checkpoint's own answers and scale_kd traces for a prompt file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `qda build`

```text
usage: qda build [-h] [--set KEY=VALUE] config

positional arguments:
  config           build config YAML (a checkpoint's resolved.yaml works too)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --set KEY=VALUE  override one key
```

### `qda plan`

```text
usage: qda plan [-h] [--set KEY=VALUE] config

positional arguments:
  config           build config YAML (a checkpoint's resolved.yaml works too)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --set KEY=VALUE  override one key
```

### `qda doctor`

```text
usage: qda doctor [-h] [--search CONFIG.yaml] [--set KEY.PATH=VALUE] [--report]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --search CONFIG.yaml  also check the prerequisites of a qda-agent search config (needs qda-
                        agent)
  --set KEY.PATH=VALUE  override one key of --search
  --report              list the environment for a bug report (versions, driver, filesystems): no
                        verdict, no paths
```

### `qda inspect`

```text
usage: qda inspect [-h] [--json] [--target TARGET] [--serve]
                   [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]
                   path

positional arguments:
  path                  checkpoint directory, .gguf file or HF repo id (org/name[@rev])

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print the report as JSON
  --target TARGET       serving target, e.g. sm90@0.33.0 (default: the card this process sees,
                        else the target the checkpoint's build.json records, else the library's)
  --serve               also load it in stock vLLM and name every tensor vLLM never read (needs a
                        card and vLLM)
  --gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION
                        the share of the card --serve lets vLLM use (default 0.85)
```

### `qda eval`

```text
usage: qda eval [-h] [--suite PRESET] [--lcb-sandbox {auto,bwrap,none}] [--format {md,html}]
                [--baseline KEY] [--resamples N] [--seed N] [--set KEY=VALUE]
                [--only KEY[/SUITE[.LABEL]]] [--server URL] [--dry-run]
                CONFIG|CKPT|RUN_DIR [CKPT|OUT ...]

Score checkpoints against their original. The first argument decides the form: a file is an eval
config (YAML); a directory holding FINAL.json is a search run (RUN_DIR); a directory holding
build.json is a checkpoint (CKPT, more may follow); `table` and `paired` print a finished eval's
results.

positional arguments:
  CONFIG|CKPT|RUN_DIR   an eval config YAML (an eval's resolved.yaml works too); a checkpoint `qda
                        build` wrote; a finished search run; or `table` / `paired`
  CKPT|OUT              more checkpoints after a first CKPT; qda eval table/paired: the eval run
                        directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --suite PRESET        CKPT and RUN_DIR: the benchmark to run, one of kl, sanity, full (the
                        original model's released card settings) or specdec; one `{suite:
                        settings}` entry also works, e.g. '{lm_eval: {tasks: [gpqa_diamond]}}'.
                        Required with CKPT; without it a RUN_DIR reports holdout KL only. Results
                        go to CKPT-eval/PRESET (change it with --set out=DIR) or
                        RUN_DIR/evaluate/PRESET
  --lcb-sandbox {auto,bwrap,none}
                        CKPT and RUN_DIR: what runs LiveCodeBench's generated programs: auto
                        (default; bubblewrap when it is installed, else stop), bwrap (require it)
                        or none (run them unsandboxed on this machine)
  --format {md,html}    qda eval table/paired: output format (default md)
  --baseline KEY        qda eval table/paired: checkpoint key to compare against
  --resamples N         qda eval paired: question resamples per interval (default: the run's
                        paired.resamples)
  --seed N              qda eval paired: RNG seed of those resamples (default: the run's
                        paired.seed)
  --set KEY=VALUE       override one key
  --only KEY[/SUITE[.LABEL]]
                        run only these jobs: a checkpoint, every part of one suite, or one part
                        (repeatable)
  --server URL          generate on a running vLLM completions server (e.g.
                        http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions) instead of starting an engine per
                        job; the transport is recorded, not digested
  --dry-run             print the jobs and which are cached; run nothing
```

```text
usage: qda decode-gguf [-h] --snapshot DIR --out DIR [--dtype {bf16,fp32}] GGUF

Decode a GGUF back to the HF checkpoint the pinned converter made it from (qwen2, qwen3, qwen3moe,
llama, gemma3, qwen35, qwen35moe).

positional arguments:
  GGUF                 the .gguf file

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit

```

### `qda fisher`

```text
usage: qda fisher [-h] {map,allocate} ...

Fisher map: what each unit's bit width costs in bits and is predicted to cost in KL, measured once per model.

positional arguments:
  {map,allocate}
    map           measure the map of a bf16 model on calibration samples
    allocate      one format per unit inside a bpw budget, as a formats: block

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit

examples:
  qda fisher map --model Qwen3.5-4B --calib calib.jsonl --menu bf16,w8a16-sym-g128,w4a16-asym-g128 \
      --samples 128 --seqlen 2048 --device cuda:0 --out map.json
  qda fisher map --model Qwen3-8B --calib calib.jsonl --menu bf16,w8a16 --out map.json  # its cards

cards: without --device the map takes the cards the model needs, from every GPU the job sees: three times the model's bf16 weight bytes plus the activation margin of a sample, in the share of the smallest visible card a map may use (0.94 of it) -- about two cards for an eight-billion-parameter model on eighty-gigabyte cards, three for a twenty-seven-billion one; the three times is the fp32 Fisher accumulator beside the bf16 model (about three times the model's weights in all, every routed-expert bank included), and a job with fewer cards is refused instead of run to an OOM
cache: a map of the same model, calibration, menu, samples and seqlen is reused from $QDA_CACHE/fisher: a repeat run prints `from cache` and the path

exit status: 0 ok, 2 refused (bad calibration file, a format the target cannot serve, a body over budget,
a job with fewer cards than the model needs)
```

#### `qda fisher map`

```text
usage: qda fisher map [-h] --model DIR --calib FILE --menu MENU [--samples SAMPLES]
                      [--seqlen SEQLEN] [--target TARGET] [--device DEVICE] [--no-cache] --out
                      FILE

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --model DIR        the bf16 original
  --calib FILE       calibration JSONL (text, messages or ids)
  --menu MENU        comma-separated formats, bf16 allowed
  --samples SAMPLES  calibration samples (default 128)
  --seqlen SEQLEN    tokens per sample (default 2048)
  --target TARGET    serving target (default: the library's)
  --device DEVICE    cpu, one GPU (cuda:0), or several (cuda:0,cuda:1,...); without --device the
                     map takes the cards the model needs, from every GPU the job sees: three times
                     the model's bf16 weight bytes plus the activation margin of a sample, in the
                     share of the smallest visible card a map may use (0.94 of it) -- about two
                     cards for an eight-billion-parameter model on eighty-gigabyte cards, three
                     for a twenty-seven-billion one; the three times is the fp32 Fisher
                     accumulator beside the bf16 model (about three times the model's weights in
                     all, every routed-expert bank included), and a job with fewer cards is
                     refused instead of run to an OOM
  --no-cache         rebuild the map even when one of these inputs is already cached
  --out FILE         the map, JSON
```

#### `qda fisher allocate`

```text
usage: qda fisher allocate [-h] --body BODY --budget-bpw BUDGET [--head-lease] MAP

positional arguments:
  MAP

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --body BODY          the row's format, every unit's start
  --budget-bpw BUDGET  bits per weight of the decoder Linears with --body (with --head-lease, the
                       head too)
  --head-lease         also give the untied output head a format: it is charged 16 bits a weight
                       and what a narrower head saves goes to the body (the search's
                       judge.head_lease); default off, the head stays as stored
```

### `qda calib`

```text
usage: qda calib [-h] {render} ...

positional arguments:
  {render}
    render    pool rows rendered with the model's own chat template, as frozen text

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

#### `qda calib render`

```text
usage: qda calib render [-h] --model MODEL [--pool POOL] --names NAMES [--rows ROWS]
                        [--samples SAMPLES] [--seqlen SEQLEN] --out OUT
                        [--thinking {keep,off,drop}] [--seed SEED]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         the model (its tokenizer and chat template)
  --pool POOL           a directory or Hub dataset REPO[@REV] (default qda-lab/qda-calibration-
                        pools)
  --names NAMES         pool files and weights, e.g. chat=3,multilingual=2
  --rows ROWS           rows of the output (or --samples with --seqlen)
  --samples SAMPLES     packed samples the build reads (with --seqlen)
  --seqlen SEQLEN       tokens per sample the build reads
  --out OUT             the JSONL file to write (refused if it exists)
  --thinking {keep,off,drop}
                        reasoning policy (default keep)
  --seed SEED           the mixing seed (default 0)
```

### `qda rotate-draft`

```text
usage: qda rotate-draft [-h] --checkpoint DIR|ID --draft DIR|ID --out DIR [--base DIR|ID]

Rotate an external speculative draft into the residual basis of a rotated checkpoint.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --checkpoint DIR|ID  a model built with `rotate`
  --draft DIR|ID       the draft model to rotate
  --out DIR            output directory (must not exist)
  --base DIR|ID        the unrotated model (default: the checkpoint's record, else the draft's
                       declared base model)

examples:
  qda rotate-draft --checkpoint qwen3.5-9b-w4a16 --draft z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash --out qwen3.5-9b-dflash-rot
  qda rotate-draft --checkpoint qwen3.8-27b-w4a16 --draft RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-speculator.dspark \
      --out qwen3.8-27b-dspark-rot

vLLM detects a DFlash draft by "dflash" in its path: keep "dflash" (or "dspark") in --out.

exit status: 0 ok, 2 refused (nothing written)
```

### `qda sensitivity`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity [-h] {plan,types,table,groups,base,read} ...

positional arguments:
  {plan,types,table,groups,base,read}
    plan                tensor payload bytes of every class at each grid type
    types               the tensor_types rules of a class allocation
    table               allocate a type per class from measured cell reads
    groups              write the derived-group cache a candidate type map expands through
    base                lay a checkpoint out one tensor class per shard, for the reads
    read                fake-quant one class at one type, score it, and write the row

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

#### `qda sensitivity plan`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity plan [-h] [--json] template

positional arguments:
  template    a bf16 GGUF template (its header is read, nothing else)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      one object per class instead of a table
```

#### `qda sensitivity types`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity types [-h] [--compact] template picks

positional arguments:
  template    the bf16 GGUF template the build will quantize
  picks       an allocation as JSON: {"picks": {"class": "type"}}

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --compact   one line instead of indented JSON
```

#### `qda sensitivity table`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity table [-h] [--baseline BASELINE] [--budget-bytes BYTES] [--floor FLOOR]
                             [--quantum QUANTUM] [--json]
                             template rows

positional arguments:
  template              a bf16 GGUF template
  rows                  JSON rows: {"class", "type", "out" | "d_kl"}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --baseline BASELINE   the bf16 read's kl; rows without d_kl subtract it
  --budget-bytes BYTES  whole-.gguf file-size budget; default: the whole frontier
  --floor FLOOR         a smaller increment counts as zero
  --quantum QUANTUM     allocation grid, in bytes
  --json
```

#### `qda sensitivity groups`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity groups [-h] --template TEMPLATE --out OUT [--json] config

positional arguments:
  config               the build config whose recipe the candidates will run (without type_map)

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --template TEMPLATE  the bf16 GGUF template the builds will quantize
  --out OUT            where to write it (typically beside the config)
  --json               print the cache instead of a summary line
```

#### `qda sensitivity base`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity base [-h] --out OUT [--max-shard MAX_SHARD] [--json] anchor

positional arguments:
  anchor                the bf16 checkpoint the reads are variants of

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT             a fresh directory for the prepared base
  --max-shard MAX_SHARD
                        shard cap, in bytes
  --json                print the base manifest
```

#### `qda sensitivity read`

```text
usage: qda sensitivity read [-h] [--class KLASS] [--type KIND] --ref REF --out OUT
                            [--subset SUBSET] [--tp TP] [--libggml LIBGGML] [--no-check] [--json]
                            base

positional arguments:
  base               a prepared base (the `base` command's directory)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --class KLASS      the tensor class; bf16 is the baseline
  --type KIND        Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0, or bf16
  --ref REF          the sealed non-GGUF reference the judge scores against
  --out OUT          a fresh directory for this read
  --subset SUBSET    the reference subset the judge screens on
  --tp TP            tensor parallel size (default 1)
  --libggml LIBGGML  a built libggml-base; Q5_K needs one
  --no-check         skip the scorer's check
  --json             print the row instead of its line
```

### `qda traces`

```text
usage: qda traces [-h] --max-tokens MAX_TOKENS --seed SEED [--rows ROWS] [--join] [--tp TP]
                  [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]
                  model prompts prefix

positional arguments:
  model                 checkpoint directory or Hub id (packed checkpoints keep their kernel
                        settings)
  prompts               JSONL of {"prompt": ...} rows
  prefix                output prefix: PREFIX-traces.jsonl, PREFIX-answers.jsonl, PREFIX-
                        generation.json

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --max-tokens MAX_TOKENS
                        completion tokens per prompt
  --seed SEED           sampling seed; change it for fresh draws
  --rows ROWS           START:STOP slice of the prompt rows (default: all)
  --join                write every answer into one text row
  --tp TP               tensor-parallel cards (default 1)
  --gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION
                        vLLM memory budget per card (default 0.85)
```

## `qda-kl`

```text
usage: qda-kl [-h] {ref,score,kl,gencheck} ...

Build a reference once per original model, then score any checkpoint against it.

positional arguments:
  {ref,score,kl,gencheck}
    ref                 build a reference for an original model
    score               score a checkpoint against a reference
    gencheck            check long generations against the original model
    kl                  one checkpoint's KL from its own original, in one command

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `qda-kl ref`

```text
usage: qda-kl ref [-h] --model MODEL --prompts PROMPTS --out OUT [--answers ANSWERS] [--seed SEED]
                  [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS] [--top-k K]
                  [--chat-template-kwargs CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS] [--sampling SAMPLING] [--tp TP]
                  [--subset NAME=FILE] [--gpu-memory-utilization FRACTION] [--serve-env JSON]
                  [--serve-args JSON] [--nccl-nvls] [--cache] [--group JSON]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         the original model: a local directory or a Hub id (REPO[@REV])
  --prompts PROMPTS     JSONL: {id, domain, prompt} or {id, domain, text}
  --out OUT
  --answers ANSWERS     answers per prompt (default 2)
  --seed SEED           seed of draw 0; draw d uses seed + d (default 17)
  --max-tokens MAX_TOKENS
                        cap of one answer (default 8192)
  --top-k K             top-k kept per position (default 128)
  --chat-template-kwargs CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS
                        JSON, e.g. {"enable_thinking": false}
  --sampling SAMPLING   JSON, e.g. {"temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95}; each field wins over the
                        model's released cards' row, which wins over its generation_config.json
  --tp TP
  --subset NAME=FILE    record a named subset of prompt ids (one per line) in the manifest, e.g.
                        search96=ids.txt
  --gpu-memory-utilization FRACTION
                        vLLM's share of the card (default 0.85); lower it when other jobs share
                        the card
  --serve-env JSON      engine environment as JSON, e.g. '{"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "false"}'
  --serve-args JSON     extra vllm.LLM arguments as JSON, e.g. '{"enable_expert_parallel": true}'
  --nccl-nvls           let the engine's ranks join NCCL's NVLS collectives (default off)
  --cache               build into the reference cache ($QDA_CACHE/kl-ref) once and make --out a
                        link to it; a later call on the same model, prompts and settings reuses it
  --group JSON          another prompt file and reference directory built in the same engine load:
                        '{"prompts": FILE, "out": DIR, "subsets": {"NAME": IDS_FILE}}' (subsets
                        optional; with --cache, a group without "out" only warms the cache)
```

### `qda-kl kl`

```text
usage: qda-kl kl [-h] [--original ORIGINAL] [--prompts PROMPTS] [--tp TP]
                 [--gpu-memory-utilization FRACTION] [--serve-env JSON] [--serve-args JSON]
                 [--nccl-nvls] [--out OUT]

options:

                        and Hub revision the checkpoint's resolved.yaml or build.json records)

  --gpu-memory-utilization FRACTION

  --serve-env JSON      engine environment as JSON, e.g. '{"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "false"}'
  --serve-args JSON     extra vllm.LLM arguments as JSON, e.g. '{"enable_expert_parallel": true}'
  --nccl-nvls           let the engine's ranks join NCCL's NVLS collectives (default off)
```


## `qda-agent`

```text
usage: qda-agent [-h] {prepare,search,status,run,gate,cand0} ...

qda-agent run CONFIG.yaml: start a search; qda doctor --search CONFIG.yaml checks the machine
first.

positional arguments:
  {prepare,search,status,run,gate,cand0}
    run                 run a search
    gate                run a search's start phase alone and print its W (no agent)
    cand0               build candidate 0 in one step and write the run config entry
    prepare             make every input of one search and its run config
    search              check the machine (qda doctor --search), then run the search
    status              print a run's progress now (the view `run` streams to stderr)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `qda-agent prepare`

```text
usage: qda-agent prepare [-h] --model MODEL --out OUT [--format FORMAT] [--cards CARDS]
                         [--budget-gpu-hours BUDGET_GPU_HOURS] [--backend BACKEND]
                         [--sign-in-dir SIGN_IN_DIR] [--sensitivity] [--dry-run]
                         [--budget-bpw N|candidate0|hf:REPO[:FILE]]
                         [--head-lease | --no-head-lease] [--calib FILE]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         a Hub id (REPO[@REVISION]) or a local model directory
  --out OUT             the directory every output goes into
  --format FORMAT       the search's format preset (default w4a16), or a spelling that names a
                        group size (w4a16-g64, w4a16-pc); a bare preset lowers its 128 only to a
                        group that stores the model
  --cards CARDS         the GPUs, comma separated (default 0); the reference reads on one of them
                        when the model fits one card, else on the most of them vLLM splits the
                        model over
  --budget-gpu-hours BUDGET_GPU_HOURS
                        the search's GPU budget (default 4)
  --backend BACKEND     the agent backend (`qda_agent.backends`), or the mapping a config holds:
                        '{name: codex, model: gpt-5.6-sol}' (default claude)
  --sign-in-dir SIGN_IN_DIR
                        the agent CLI's config dir that holds its sign-in
                        (agent.backend.sign_in_dir; default ~/.claude)
  --sensitivity         GGUF only: measure the class sensitivity sweep and give candidate 0 its
                        measured type map (off by default; a few GPU-hours)
  --dry-run             print the plan and the disk estimate; run nothing
  --budget-bpw N|candidate0|hf:REPO[:FILE]
                        the size the search must stay within: N bits per quantized weight,
                        candidate 0's own price, or a published checkpoint's (a GGUF file's bytes,
                        or a compressed-tensors/GPTQ/AWQ checkpoint's bpw, read without
                        downloading its weights); default w4a16 4.4, w4a8 4.4, w3a16 3.4, w4a4
                        4.8, and candidate 0's size for gguf-q4km
  --head-lease, --no-head-lease
                        for a search that may also shrink the output head: the bits a narrower
                        head saves are lent to the body under --budget-bpw (judge.head_lease);
                        default on for w4a4, off otherwise; not for gguf-q4km
  --calib FILE          candidate 0's and the search's calibration file (JSONL), used as is
                        instead of the public pool mix
```

### `qda-agent run`

```text
usage: qda-agent run [-h] [--set KEY.PATH=VALUE] config

positional arguments:
  config                the run YAML, or a run's resolved.yaml to repeat it

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --set KEY.PATH=VALUE  override one key of the config (the value is YAML); repeatable
```

### `qda-agent gate`

```text
usage: qda-agent gate [-h] [--set KEY.PATH=VALUE] config

positional arguments:
  config                the run YAML the search will launch with

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --set KEY.PATH=VALUE
```

### `qda-agent cand0`

```text
usage: qda-agent cand0 [-h] [--method {gptq,awq,gguf-q4km}] [--gsq] [--out OUT]
                       [--cards CARDS [CARDS ...]] [--recipe-only] [--in-place] [--force]
                       [--set KEY.PATH=VALUE]
                       config

positional arguments:
  config                the run YAML the search will launch with

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --method {gptq,awq,gguf-q4km}
                        the build method (default gptq)
  --gsq                 refine the method's codes with qda-quant's gsq step (after it)
  --out OUT             the checkpoint directory (default: <config dir>/cand0-<method>)
  --cards CARDS [CARDS ...]
                        cards to build on, as CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: 0,1 or 0 1 (default: every
                        visible card)
  --recipe-only         print the recipe and stop (no build)
  --in-place            rewrite the config itself instead of a new file
  --force               with --in-place: rewrite even a file with comments
  --set KEY.PATH=VALUE  override one key of the run config (the value is YAML); repeatable
```
